_about: JoyPro's terms and how each language says them (docs/localization.md). Every translation uses these words for these concepts, so the same thing has one name on every page. glossary.json holds the terms of all languages; this file is the English source with the meaning of each term.
rules: Short UI labels: buttons and column headers as short as the language allows (German, Finnish and others run long: prefer the shorter common word, never cut words).
Buttons and menu items in the platform style of Windows in that language (German: infinitive 'Speichern'; French: infinitive 'Enregistrer'; Japanese/Chinese: short verb noun).

Keep placeholders {0}, {1}, {0:F1} exactly; they may move within the sentence. Keep leading and trailing spaces, line breaks (\n), and the punctuation at the start/end of fragments (' · ', '; ', ' (').

Never translate: JoyPro, JoyPro2, game names (DCS World, IL-2 Sturmovik, War Thunder, Star Citizen, Microsoft Flight Simulator, X-Plane, Falcon BMS, Arma, Elite Dangerous, Nuclear Option, WARDOGS, Hell Let Loose...), product names (vJoy, HidHide, ViGEmBus, Steam, GitHub, Windows, TrackIR, Thrustmaster, Warthog, Virpil, VKB, Winwing...), file names, paths, keys (Ctrl+Z, Esc), input ids (JOY_BTN5, JOY_BTN_POV1_U, KEY_...), engine options (--dry-run), 'DB', 'HUD', 'FFB', 'BYOJ', 'GGUF', 'llama-server'.
Game command names stay as the game names them: quoted examples like 'Pitch', 'Collective', 'Gear Up/Down' stay in English.
Menu paths (Settings > Games, More > Rename...) use the translated labels of those pages and buttons, with ' > ' kept.
Say 'device' (the controller hardware) unless the English explicitly says stick, throttle, pedals, panel or gamepad.

Address the user the way Windows does in that language: German 'Sie', French 'vous', Italian/Spanish/Portuguese neutral or formal imperative as in Windows, Nordic languages and Dutch the usual informal 'du'/'je'; labels and buttons without address (German infinitive 'Profil öffnen'). Japanese: polite です/ます in sentences, short nouns in labels. Korean: 합니다/하세요 style in sentences. Chinese: neutral, no 您 overuse.

terms.note: JoyPro's core concept: one named function (e.g. 'Gear Up/Down') linking the matching command of several games/aircraft; you bind a relation once and it is exported to every game. Noun. Plural 'relations'.
Noun: one input (button/axis/hat, maybe with modifiers) assigned to a relation. Plural 'binds'. Like 'key binding'/'assignment'.
Verb: assign an input to a relation ('Bind here', 'bound', 'unbound'/'free').
Verb: remove the bind of a relation.
A button held down to give other buttons a second meaning (like Shift). Plural 'modifiers'.
A game controller (stick, throttle, pedals, button box, gamepad) connected to the PC. The general word; never 'joystick'.
One button, axis or hat direction of a device.
An analog control of a device (pitch, throttle lever). Plural 'axes'.
A digital control of a device.
A POV hat switch (4/8-way thumb switch) on a stick. Often kept as 'Hat'/'POV hat'.
The JoyPro file holding all relations, binds and modifiers (.pr0file).
A supported simulator/game.
A plane or helicopter (a DCS module etc.). Singular and plural same in English.
A control command/action as the game defines it (game data). 'command list': the game's list of commands JoyPro builds from the installation.
Same as command: a game's control action.
Verb/noun: read the binds made in a game into JoyPro.
Verb/noun: write JoyPro's binds into the game's control files.
A tag that groups relations (e.g. 'Weapons', 'Radio').
Verb: capture an input by pressing it on the device.
The Layout page: a picture of a device with its inputs labeled.
A printable picture of a device with what each input does.
An axis response curve (axis tuning).
Axis dead zone around the centre.
FFB: motors in the stick push back.
vJoy: a software joystick JoyPro feeds from your devices. Here 'joystick' is the product type and stays.
The Settings page; also 'setting' (one option).
A saved copy of a game's control files.
A saved state of the profile in its History.
The profile's list of earlier versions (top bar 'History').
Verb: revert the last change (Ctrl+Z).
Verb/noun: a newer JoyPro, or rebuilding a game's command list after a game update.
The Windows notification area (system tray) next to the clock.
Verb: JoyPro watches a game's control files for changes ('Watch game configs').
An image of a device (photo or JoyPro's drawing).
JoyPro's own line drawing of a device.
An aircraft's cockpit (Cockpits page).
In-game text overlay showing presses; HUD = the on-screen display of binds.
Verb: JoyPro proposes matching commands ('Suggested for this relation').
The first page (dashboard) 'Start'.
The panel showing the engine's text output.
Only where the English explicitly says stick (the flight stick).
The throttle device or lever.
Rudder pedals.
The exchangeable handle of a stick on its base.
The stick base a grip sits on.
